questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

All apples are oranges.

Some oranges are bananas.

All bananas are kiwis.

**Conclusions:**

I. Some oranges are kiwis.

II. Some oranges are apples.

III. Some apples are bananas.

options.text: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow

questions.solution:
Statements:

All apples are oranges.

Some oranges are bananas.

All bananas are kiwis.

The Venn diagram as per the given statements:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d6c08cc3c264dbb8e4ef1519d973a9fefbe2da5d81ffa855c9726283c394e84a.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some oranges are kiwis. →** True **(Because some oranges are bananas and all bananas are kiwis, which means some oranges are kiwis is definitely true)

II. Some oranges are apples. → **True** (Because all apples are oranges, which means some oranges are apples is definitely true)

III. Some apples are bananas. → **False** (There is no direct relation between apples and bananas, so it can be possible but not definitely true)

Hence, the correct answer is **"Only conclusions I and II follow".**

questions.question:
Which of the mathematical signs should be interchanged in the below equation to make it mathematically correct?

12 + 112 ÷ 16 - 8 × 64 = 140
questions.solution:
Here, we use the BODMAS table given below:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/776aca73050e2d15fdc3daba520ead29df1123b2c3ef98d848cb946a081897d6.png] 

Given:

⇒ 12 + 112 ÷ 16 - 8 × 64 = 140

(1) **+ and -**

⇒ 12 + 112 ÷ 16 - 8 × 64 = 140

After interchanging the signs:

⇒ 12 - __**112 ÷ 16**__ + 8 × 64

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 12 - 7 + __**8 × 64**__

⇒ 12 - 7 + 512

⇒ 524 - 7 = 517

Here, the equation is not satisfied.

(2) **÷ and ×**

⇒ 12 + 112 ÷ 16 - 8 × 64 = 140

After interchanging the signs:

⇒ 12 + 112 × 16 - __**8 ÷ 64**__

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 12 +** __112 × 16__** - 0.125

⇒ 12 + 1792 - 0.125

⇒ 1804 - 0.125 = 1803.875

Here, the equation is not satisfied.

(3) **+ and ×**

⇒ 12 + 112 ÷ 16 - 8 × 64 = 140

After interchanging the signs:

⇒ 12 × __**112 ÷ 16**__ - 8 + 64

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ __**12 × 7**__ - 8 + 64

⇒ 84 - 8 + 64

⇒ 148 - 8 = **140**

**⇒ '12 × 112 ÷ 16 - 8 + 64 = 140'**

Here, the equation is **satisfied.**

(4) **+ and ÷**

⇒ 12 + 112 ÷ 16 - 8 × 64 = 140

After interchanging the signs:

⇒ __**12 ÷ 112**__ + 16 - 8 × 64

Apply BODMAS rule:

⇒ 0.107 + 16 - __**8 × 64**__

⇒ 0.107 + 16 - 512

⇒ 16.107 - 512 = (-495.89)

Here, the equation is not satisfied.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option (3)".

questions.question: Famous ruler Kanishka belonged to the ______ dynasty.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Kushan__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kanishka belonged to the Kushan dynasty__.
 
• The kushan dynasty was founded by Kujūla Kadphises.
 
• Kanishka ruled around the 1st century CE and was the greatest king of the Kushan dynasty.
 
• At the time of Kanishka, kushan rule was spread over the northern part of the Indian subcontinent, Afghanistan, and possibly areas of Central Asia north of the Kashmir region.
 
• He is also remembered as a great patron of Buddhism.
 
• He studied Buddhism under the Buddhist poet Ashvaghosha.
 
• The Fourth Buddhist Council was also convened under his patronage in Kashmir.
 
• That council compiled The Great Commentary on Abhidharma.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The Kushanas:

 
 
• The first Kushana dynasty was founded by Kujula Kadphises.
 
• Vima Kadphises issued gold coins in India.
 
• Kanishka founded the second Kushana dynasty.
 
• Their capitals were at Peshawar and Mathura.
 
• The most famous Kushana ruler was Kanishka, he was also known as ‘*Second Ashoka*’.
 
• He started an era in 78 AD which is now known as the Saka Era and is used by the Government of India.
 
• Kanishka was a great patron of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• During his reign, the 4th Buddhist Council was held in Kundalavana, Kashmir where the doctrines of the Mahayana form of Buddhism were finalized.
 
• The last great Kushana ruler was Vasudeva I.
 
• The Kushanas were the first rulers in India to issue gold coins on a wide scale.

questions.question: All executive actions of the Government of a state shall be expressed to be taken in the name of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Governor.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] __Key Points__

Governor:

__
 
• The Governor’s appointment, his powers and everything related to the office of Governor has been discussed under Article 153 to Article 162 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The role of the Governor is quite similar to that of the President of India.
 
• The Governor performs the same duties as of President, but for the State.
 
• Governor stands as the executive head of a State and the working remains the same as of the office of the President of India.
 
• All the executive action of a state government shall be exercised by order in the name of the Governor.
 
• Under the Constitution of India, the governing machinery is the same as that of the Central Government.
 
• It is stated that the Governor has a dual role.
 
 
• He is the constitutional head of the state, bound by the advice of his council of ministers.
 
• He functions as a vital link between the Union Government and the State Government.
 
 
 
• The term of the governor's office is normally 5 years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• According to Article 164 in the Indian Constitution, Governor appoints Chief Minister.
 
• However, the Governor cannot appoint any random person as the Chief Minister but has to follow a provision.
 
• A leader of the party that has got the majority share of votes in the assembly elections, is appointed as the Chief Minister of the state. 

 
• 
 
 
• Article 75:- The PM shall be appointed by the President and the other Ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the PM.

 
 
• The total number of ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the COM, shall not exceed 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.
 
• A minister who is not a member of the Parliament (either house) for any period of six consecutive months shall cease to be a minister.
 
 
 
• Article 75 clearly states that the COM is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha.
 
 
• This means that all the ministers own joint responsibility to the Lok Sabha for all their acts of omission and commission.
 
 
 
• Article 75 also contains the principle of individual responsibility.
 
 
• It states that the ministers hold office during the pleasure of the President, which means that the President can remove a minister even at a time when the COM enjoys the confidence of the Lok Sabha.
 
• However, the President removes a minister only on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
 
 
 
 
• The council of Ministers comes into existence after the Ministers have taken the oath to their respective offices.

questions.question: Battle of Buxar was fought in _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __1764.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] Key Points__

__
 
• The Battle of Buxar was fought on October 22, 1764 AD.
 
• It was fought between the joint forces of the Nawab Mir Qasim of Bengal, Nawab Sujauddaula of Awadh and the Mughal ruler Shah Alam II and the British.
 
• The United Indian Army was defeated in the Battle of Buxar fought on October 22, 1764.
 
• In 1765, Suja-ud-daulah and Shah Alam signed a treaty with Company Governor Clive in Allahabad.
 
• Under this treaty, the company was given civil rights in Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa, which authorized the company to collect revenue from these areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information__ The reasons for battle were:

 
• Mir Qasim wanted to be independent and shifted his capital to Munger Fort from Calcutta. 
 
• These factors fuelled the English to overthrow him and war broke out between Mir Kasim and the Company in 1763.
 
• Participants of the Battle of Buxar were:
 
 
• Mir Qasim – (Administering Bengal in place of Mir Jafar – Nawab of Bengal)
 
• Shuja-Ud-Daulah – Nawab of Awadh (Oudh)
 
• Shah Alam II – Mughal Emperor
 
 

Result of the Battle of Buxar:

 
• Mir Jafar (Nawab of Bengal) handed over districts of Midnapore, Burdwan, and Chittagong to the English for the maintenance of their army.
 
• The English were also permitted duty-free trade in Bengal, except for a duty of two per cent on salt.
 
• Clive made political settlements with Emperor Shah Alam II and Shuja-Ud-Daula of Awadh in the Treaty of Allahabad.

questions.question: Vishu is predominantly celebrated in which of the following states of India?

• Vishu festival falls on the first day of the Malayali month of Medam, which occurs on either April 14 or 15 on the Gregorian calendar.​
 
• Vishu festival__
 __
 
• It is celebrated in Kerala as the harvest festival and the astrological New Year of the Malayalis.
 
• Vishu indicates the movement of the sun to Aries or the Mesha Rashi and marks the day from which the farmers begin the plowing of land and other agricultural activities.
 
• In Sanskrit, Vishu means equal, which implies the day with an equal number of hours of day and night or the equinox.
 
• The day of Mesha Sankranti or Mesha Sankramam, Vishu is a family festival.
 
• It is a period dedicated to Lord Vishnu and is celebrated by worshipping Lord Vishnu and Lord Krishna.
 
• Vishu Kani, Vishu Kaineettam, and Vishubhalam are the three most important aspects of the Vishu celebrations.
 
 
• As per the religious faith of the people on the previous night of the Vishu festival, a Vishu Kani in the prayer room or worship area of the house before the idol of Lord Vishnu and Lord Krishna by the eldest lady of the house.
 
• Vishu Kani is regarded as the symbol of good luck and prosperity by all Hindu Malayalis.
 
 
 
• It marks the beginning of the spring season.

• ** A trade surplus means that a nation is exporting more goods and services than it is importing.**
 
• This results in an inflow of foreign currency, which can be used to** pay off debt or invested in the economy.**
 
• Positive net exports also indicate that a nation is competitive in the global market and has a comparative advantage in certain industries. This can lead to increased employment and economic growth.
 
• On the other hand, a trade deficit means that a nation is importing more than it is exporting, resulting in an outflow of currency. This can lead to a decrease in foreign reserves and potentially weaken the national currency.
 
• ** A trade surplus is not always desirable,** as it can lead to trade tensions with other nations and may cause the domestic industry to become too reliant on exports.A trade deficit may not always be a bad thing, as it can help a nation access goods and services that it cannot produce domestically and may stimulate economic growth through increased consumption

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] Additional Information____ Some additional points on trade surpluses and deficits:__

 
• Balance of Payments: The terms trade surplus and deficit are part of a country's balance of payments, which includes not only trade in goods and services but also capital transfers and financial transactions. While a trade surplus adds to the balance of payments, a deficit subtracts from it.
 
• Economic Performance: A trade surplus is often seen as a sign of economic strength, and a deficit as a sign of weakness. However, this is an oversimplification. For example, a trade deficit can occur during periods of strong economic growth, when a country's businesses and consumers are buying more goods from overseas. Conversely, a trade surplus could occur during an economic downturn, when there is lower domestic demand for foreign goods.
 
• Currency Implications: Trade balances can affect the value of a country's currency in the foreign exchange markets. A sustained trade surplus can put upward pressure on a country's currency value, while a sustained trade deficit can put downward pressure on it.
 
• Impact on Domestic Industries: Constant trade deficits may harm domestic industries as they have to compete with cheaper or better foreign goods. On the other hand, continuous trade surpluses might lead to protectionist policies which can hinder competition and innovation in the long run.
 
• Debt Levels: Countries with large and persistent trade deficits often need to borrow from other countries to finance their deficits. This can increase the country's overall debt levels and make it more vulnerable to economic crises.
 
• Politics and Trade Policy: Trade surpluses and deficits can have significant impacts on politics and the development of trade policies. For instance, countries facing trade deficits may be more inclined to implement protectionist policies, such as tariffs and quotas, to protect domestic industries. On the other hand, those with trade surpluses might face pressure from other nations to open their markets more.

questions.question: 40 men can complete a work in 15 days. They started working, and after 5 days 10 more men joined them. In how many days will the total work be completed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = 40 × 15 = 600 man-days.

Remaining work after 5 days = 600 − (40 × 5) = 400 man-days.

Current workforce after 10 men join = 40 + 10 = 50 men.

Time required for the remaining work = 400 ÷ 50 = 8 days.

Total time to complete the work = 5 days + 8 days = 13 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

40 men can complete the work in 15 days.

After 5 days of working, 10 more men joined.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Time taken by 40 men to finish the whole work = 15 days.

⇒ Since time is inversely proportional to the number of men, time taken by 10 men = 15 × (40 ÷ 10) = 60 days.

⇒ Let's use the LCM method to find the total work units and individual group efficiencies:

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 40 Men
 15
 60
 4
 
 

 10 Men
 60
 1
 
 

⇒ Total efficiency of 50 men (40 + 10) = 4 + 1 = 5 units/day.

⇒ Work completed by 40 men in the first 5 days = Efficiency × Days = 4 × 5 = 20 units.

⇒ Remaining work = Total Work − Completed Work = 60 − 20 = 40 units.

⇒ Time taken by 50 men to complete the remaining work = Remaining Work ÷ Total Efficiency = 40 ÷ 5 = 8 days.

⇒ Total time to complete the whole work = Initial 5 days + 8 days = 13 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 13 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

MDH Concept

For a group of men working, the relationship is given by (M₁ × D₁ × H₁) ÷ W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂) ÷ W₂, where M = Men, D = Days, H = Hours, and W = Work.

Total Work Concept

Total Work = Number of Workers × Number of Days. This remains constant if the required task is the same, meaning more workers will always take proportionally fewer days (Inverse Proportion).

Alternate Day Work

If two workers or groups work on alternate days, calculate the combined work done in a single 2-day cycle to find out how many full cycles are needed to reach the total work.

questions.question: A and B working together can finish a project in 16 days while B alone can do it in 24 days. In how many days can A alone finish the project?
questions.solution:
**Given**

A and B can finish the work in 16 days.

B can finish the work alone in 24 days.

**Concept:** Work = rate × time

Solution:

⇒ Work done by A and B in one day = 1/16

⇒ Work done by B in one day = 1/24

⇒ Work done by A in one day = 1/16 - 1/24 = 1/48

⇒ So, A alone can finish the work in 48 days.

**Therefore, A alone can finish the project in 48 days.**

questions.question: A policeman spots a thief 120 m ahead, immediately the policeman starts chasing the thief. The policeman runs 26 m in a minute and the thief runs 20 m in a minute. In what time will the policeman catch the thief?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Distance between policeman and thief = 120 m

Policeman's speed = 26 m/min

Thief's speed = 20 m/min

**Concept:**

Relative speed and time = distance/speed

Solution:

⇒ Relative speed = 26 m/min - 20 m/min = 6 m/min

⇒ Time = 120 m / 6 m/min = 20 minutes

**Therefore, the policeman will catch the thief in 20 minutes.**

questions.question: A thief is observed by a policeman from a distance of 420 m. The thief starts running and the policeman chases him. The policeman and the thief run at a speed of 25 km/h and 20 km/h, respectively. What is the distance between them after three minutes?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Initial distance = 420 m

Policeman's speed = 25 km/h

Thief's speed = 20 km/h

Time = 3 min

**Concept:**

Relative speed and distance = speed × time

Solution:

⇒ Convert speeds from km/h to m/min: Policeman's speed = 25 × 1000/60 = 416.67 m/min, Thief's speed = 20 × 1000/60 = 333.33 m/min

⇒ Relative speed = 416.67 m/min - 333.33 m/min = 83.33 m/min

⇒ Distance covered in 3 min = 83.33 m/min × 3 min = 250 m

⇒ Remaining distance = 420 m - 250 m = 170 m

**Therefore, the distance between them after three minutes is 170 m.**

If the LCM of the first 110 natural numbers is N, then find the LCM of the first 115 natural numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The LCM of the first n natural numbers is the product of the highest prime powers ≤ n.

When extending the LCM from 110 to 115, we only look for new prime powers in the range 111 to 115.

The new numbers added are 111, 112, 113, 114, and 115.

113 is the only new prime number, and there are no higher powers of smaller primes (like 2⁷ or 3⁵).

Therefore, we just multiply the previous LCM (N) by 113.

**∴ The correct answer is 113N.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM(1, 2, ..., 110) = N

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM(1, 2, ..., 115) = LCM(N, 111, 112, 113, 114, 115)

⇒ Let us write the prime factorization of the new terms:

⇒ 111 = 3¹ × 37¹

⇒ 112 = 2⁴ × 7¹

⇒ 113 = 113¹ (Prime)

⇒ 114 = 2¹ × 3¹ × 19¹

⇒ 115 = 5¹ × 23¹

⇒ N already contains the highest powers of all primes ≤ 110.

⇒ Max power of 3 in N is 3⁴ = 81 and 37 is 37¹ → 111 completely divides N.

⇒ Max power of 2 in N is 2⁶ = 64 and 7 is 7² = 49 → 112 completely divides N.

⇒ Max powers of 19 and 23 are 19¹ and 23¹ → 114 and 115 completely divide N.

⇒ 113 is a prime number strictly greater than 110, so it is not present as a factor in N.

⇒ Required LCM = N × 113 = 113N

**∴ The correct answer is 113N.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM of Consecutive Numbers

The LCM of the first n natural numbers is formed by multiplying the highest power of every prime number that is less than or equal to n.

Extending LCM to Larger Ranges

To find the LCM of the first n+k numbers when the LCM of the first n numbers is known, simply multiply the old LCM by any prime numbers or new higher powers of primes that occur within the range (n, n+k].

Identifying New Prime Powers

If a composite number added to the range is made strictly of prime powers already smaller than n, it will not change the overall LCM. Only new prime numbers (like 113) or prime powers exceeding the previous maximums will affect it.

questions.question:
A shopkeeper is selling a gift packet of fruits in which he is mixing apples and mangoes. The packet contains a total of 12 kg of fruits at an average rate of 100 per kg. In the packet there are 8 kg of apples at the rate of ₹90 per kg, while there are 4 kg of mangoes at the rate of X per kg. Find the value of 'X'.

Note: All other charges are to be ignored for packing.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Total weight of fruits = 12 kg

Total cost = 12 kg × ₹100/kg = ₹1200

Weight of apples = 8 kg, cost = 8 kg × ₹90/kg = ₹720

Weight of mangoes = 4 kg

**Concept:**

Average cost calculation

Solution:

⇒ Cost of mangoes = total cost - cost of apples = ₹1200 - ₹720 = ₹480

⇒ Cost per kg of mangoes = total cost of mangoes/weight of mangoes = ₹480/4 kg = ₹120/kg

**Therefore, the cost of mangoes is ₹120 per kg.**

questions.question: The total surface area of a sphere is 22176 cm². The diameter of the sphere is:
questions.solution:
**Given**

Total surface area of the sphere = 22176 cm²

**Concept:**

Surface area of a sphere = 4πr², and Diameter = 2r

Solution:

⇒ 4πr² = 22176 cm²

⇒ r² = 22176 / (4π)

⇒ r = sqrt(22176 / (4π))

⇒ r = 42 cm

⇒ Diameter = 2r ≈ 84 cm

**Therefore, the diameter of the sphere is 84 cm.**

questions.question: A sum of money becomes Rs.4,900 in 3 years and Rs.6,400 in 5 years on compound interest, compounded annually. Find the rate of interest p.a.
questions.solution:
**Given**

Compound interest for 3 years = Rs. 4900

Compound interest for 5 years = Rs. 6400

**Concept:**

The formula for compound interest A = P(1 + r/n)⁽ⁿt⁾, and that the difference in compound interest for two periods is the compound interest for the period in between.

Solution:

⇒ Compound interest for the period from the 3rd year to the 5th year = Rs. 6400 - Rs. 4900 = Rs. 1500

⇒ This amount is the interest for 2 years on the amount of Rs. 4900.

⇒ Using the compound interest formula, we have 4900(1 + r/100)² = 6400.

⇒ Solve for r to get r = 14(2)/(7)% per annum.

**Therefore, the rate of interest per annum is 14(2)/(7)%.**

questions.question: If 12 men can build a wall 60 metres long in 5 days, then what length of a similar wall can be built by 24 men in 2 days?
questions.solution:
**Given**

12 men build a 60-meter wall in 5 days.

**Concept:**

The work done is proportional to the number of men and the number of days.

Solution:

⇒ 12 men × 5 days = 60 meters.

⇒ 1 man × 1 day = 60 meters/(12 × 5)

⇒ 24 men × 2 days = 24 × 2 × (60 meters/(12 × 5)) = 48 meters.

**Therefore, 24 men can build a 48-meter wall in 2 days.**

questions.question: In 90 litres of a mixture of milk and water, the ratio of milk and water is 4 ∶ 1. How much water should be added in the mixture so that the ratio of milk to water becomes 3 ∶ 1?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Initial Milk : Water = 4 : 1

Final Milk : Water = 3 : 1

Since only water is added, make the milk ratio parts equal by multiplying initial ratio by 3 and final by 4.

Initial = 12 : 3 (Total = 15 parts = 90 litres → 1 part = 6 litres)

Final = 12 : 4 (Water added = 4 − 3 = 1 part)

**∴ The correct answer is 6 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total initial mixture = 90 litres

Initial ratio of milk to water = 4 : 1

Final ratio of milk to water = 3 : 1

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c4925b01db38b02f21ae19bff7d15e85c5e15142cd4a21f2620d710b2515bd6a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total initial parts = 4 + 1 = 5 parts

⇒ Initial quantity of milk = (4 / 5) × 90 = 72 litres

⇒ Initial quantity of water = (1 / 5) × 90 = 18 litres

⇒ Let x litres of water be added to the mixture.

⇒ New quantity of water = (18 + x) litres

⇒ Since no milk is added, the milk quantity remains strictly 72 litres.

⇒ The new ratio of milk to water is 3 : 1

⇒ 72 / (18 + x) = 3 / 1

⇒ 3 × (18 + x) = 72

⇒ 54 + 3x = 72

⇒ 3x = 72 − 54 = 18

⇒ x = 6

**∴ The correct answer is 6 litres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Component Method

When a pure component (like water) is added to or removed from a mixture, the total quantity of the other component (like milk) remains completely constant. You can simply equalize the constant component parts in the before and after ratios to instantly find the change in the added component parts.

Alligation Method

This problem can also be solved using alligation on water concentration. Initial mixture has 20% (1/5) water, added pure water is 100%, and final mixture has 25% (1/4) water. The ratio of initial mixture to pure water will be (100 − 25) : (25 − 20) = 75 : 5 = 15 : 1.

Mixture Replacement Formula

If a part of the mixture is removed and identically replaced with water, the concentration of milk after n replacements is given by: Final Milk = Initial Milk × (1 − Replaced Quantity / Total Volume)ⁿ.
</p
